instructions.question: Which effort level does the Human Design report-production job described in `action` need? The jobs produce long personal readings for paying clients: an author writes a full report from a complete packet (exact chart data, a long prompt, a template, a style guide and reference works it reads passage by passage); the same author repairs named defects or checks the published document against its source; a controller session prepares inputs, calls live chart and geocoding services with real keys, dispatches authors, runs acceptance checks, publishes and files. The levels are ordered by what a miss costs and by how much later work rests on the job, not by length alone. Read three signals in the description: (1) what a miss costs: a slip the next check catches; a wrong or unsupported statement that a client reads and acts on; or a wrong chart fact, template structure or setup that every later section, composite and report inherits; (2) whether a gate still stands between this job and the client (deterministic mechanical checks, full-source acceptance, a read-back check, a QA pass) or this job is itself the last check; (3) whether the object is new (the first report of its type on this platform, a new template or prompt version, the first live production run) or a repeat on an accepted template and accepted inputs. Place the job by these three signals only, not by whether the work should be split across several independent agents.
instructions.tradeoff: Each level costs more time and tokens than the one below and buys less per step. On an independent knowledge-work evaluation (blind-graded professional tasks, Elo), the lower-cost model scores 1235, 1586, 1707, 1837 and 1866 across the five levels at $0.21, $0.86, $1.54, $4.21 and $8.92 and about 1, 3, 5, 12 and 20 minutes per task; the most capable model scores 1469, 1549, 1635, 1735 and 1758 at $1.43, $2.18, $3.48, $7.22 and $9.77 and about 3, 5, 7, 13 and 17 minutes. Reading long documents barely changes with the level: 81 to 85% on a long-context reasoning test for both models at every level. So the upper levels are earned by stakes, novelty and dependence, not by length; a level too high wastes a multiple of the cost and time, and a level too low risks the miss the levels exist to prevent.

criteria: low: the cheapest level, for steps whose miss costs almost nothing and on which nothing later rests: recording a delivery date or a link, relaying a message, filing a report that has already passed its checks, running a named script, renaming files. On the knowledge-work evaluation the lower-cost model scores 1235 here against 1586 one level up, and the most capable model 1469 against 1549, so this level is for work that needs no judgement, not for cheap judgement.

medium: bounded work inside a written checklist or a named fix, where the next check catches a miss and little rests on this job alone: correcting a typo or a caption whose section and defect are named, with the deterministic checks re-run afterwards; filling template fields from accepted data; comparing a published document against its source with a checklist while a deterministic comparison also runs; summarising a run's results. The lower-cost model defaults here: 1586 at $0.86 and about 3 minutes per task. Checklist reviews are weak on their own: in one study a review in the authoring session scored F1 22% and a fresh-session review 29% on planted errors, and omissions were caught only 14 to 21% of the time, so a deterministic check, not this level, is the real gate for such work.

high: real judgement with moderate stakes, where a later gate still stands between this job and the client: a repair pass that fixes defects named at acceptance, each with its section, failed requirement and evidence; reviewing such a repair; drafting a short focused component for a returning client on an accepted template; diagnosing why a check failed. The most capable model defaults here (1635 at $3.48 per task); the lower-cost model reaches 1707 at $1.54. Repair against named defects is the case where self-correction works, because the defects arrive with their locations: given the location, models fixed 18 to 44 points more of the wrong answers. Practitioner tests of both models recommend drafting long prose at this level or above.

extra high: long, complex, client-facing judgement where a miss reaches the client or misleads later work, with acceptance and QA still after it: writing a full 40-page reading or a two-person composite of a type already produced here, on the accepted template, from a complete packet; a routine production controller run over several reports lasting more than half an hour. Cost roughly doubles over high: the lower-cost model scores 1837 at $4.21 and about 12 minutes per task (130 Elo over high), the most capable 1735 at $7.22 (100 over high); on an independent office-deliverables evaluation (memos, decks, spreadsheets) the lower-cost model rises from 1689 at high to 1768 here.

max: the deepest reasoning level, for work where a miss is expensive or everything after it inherits the result: the first report of a new type, template or prompt version on this platform for a real client, whose structure later reports copy; the first live production run with real chart and geocoding calls; interpretation that must reconcile conflicting sources where no later check can judge the result; root-cause analysis after a repair has already failed. It buys little on average: the lower-cost model gains 29 Elo over extra high at 2.1 times the cost and 1.7 times the time per task, the most capable model 23 Elo at 1.35 times the cost; on a closed-book knowledge test the share of unknown answers the lower-cost model gets wrong instead of declining falls from 66% to 59% at this level, while the most capable model's rises from 71% to 73%; in a review benchmark this level caught 10 of 13 hard defects against 8, while precision fell from 67% to 52%. Reserve it for first-of-a-kind or irreversible work.

instructions.question: Should the Human Design report-production job described in `action` be done by several independent agents, each taking or checking one part of the work, rather than by one session alone? This is separate from how much reasoning each part needs.
instructions.tradeoff: Claim-by-claim checking is cheap and close to human agreement (72% agreement with human raters on about 16,000 facts, at about $0.19 per response); one fresh review by the same model plus one by a different model caught 57% of planted errors against 43% for two reviews by the same model. Gains plateau at a few independent reviewers, and multi-agent setups used 15 to 80 times the tokens of one agent, so several agents are for independence a single reader cannot supply, not for routine reports or listed repairs.

criteria.true: The job splits into many separate parts of the same kind that independent checkers can each take on in parallel without needing one another's results.
criteria.false: The job is one connected piece of work that one careful pass must follow as a whole: writing one report, repairing named defects in one report, checking one published document against its source, recording or filing, or a controller run whose steps depend on each other.

instructions.question: Which model should run the Human Design report-production job described in `action`, at whatever effort level it needs?
instructions.tradeoff: Both are frontier models with the same five effort levels, and either can run as several independent agents (in Claude Code, both support the many-agent workflow setting at every effort level). The most capable model costs 2.5 times as much per token ($10 and $50 per million input and output tokens against $4 and $20) and generates about 55 to 64 tokens per second against about 80 to 97. On independent knowledge-work and document evaluations the lower-cost model leads from the middle level up: blind-graded professional tasks 1866 against 1758 Elo at max and 1837 against 1735 at extra high, where it costs $4.21 per task against $7.22; office deliverables 1807 against 1676; multi-step professional agent tasks 73.5 against 68.6. The most capable model leads at the lowest level (1469 against 1235) and on single-pass expert writing from supplied source documents: expert tasks with source documents 73.8 against 65.8; legal deliverables from case files with every criterion met 14 to 17% against 8%; legal research 55.3 against 50.5; tax work 77.6 against 70.5. Writing quality is close: the most capable model leads a judged creative-writing test (2162 against 2050) and a long-form test (85.3 against 84.6, neither degrading over eight chapters), while the lower-cost model leads crowd votes on creative writing, long queries and instruction following (1516 against 1482, 1526 against 1510, 1517 against 1498). Reading long documents is a tie (81 to 85% for both). On a closed-book knowledge test at max, the lower-cost model answers wrongly instead of declining on 59% of the questions it does not know, against 73%. Reviewers found the most capable model stayed faithful to source material but overran explicit length limits, and the lower-cost model, as an editor, sometimes produced a revision that ignored its own diagnosis.

most_capable_model.what: Work where the depth of one pass of expert synthesis from source material decides the outcome and later work builds on it: the first report of a new type, template or prompt version on this platform; a two-person composite whose relationship mechanics must be reconciled across both charts when that report type has not been produced here before; interpretation that weighs conflicting statements across several reference works where no later check can judge it; a client's open questions whose framing is not given; or work on which the lower-cost model at a higher level has already fallen short.
most_capable_model.not_for: Work on an accepted template and accepted inputs with acceptance and QA behind it, or work with a written checklist or named defects: standard readings and composites of a type already produced here, repairs of named defects, checks of a published document against its source, controller steps that run written scripts, recording and filing. There the 2.5 times price and slower turns buy little, and on independent knowledge-work evaluations the lower-cost model at extra high already outscores this one at max.
examples: Write the first parent-child composite report produced on this platform, for a paying client, from a complete packet
Reconcile two reference works that disagree about a gate's meaning before a report section is written
Rewrite a report section after two repairs by the lower-cost model failed acceptance

strong_lower_cost_model.what: Well-specified report work that a strong model completes reliably, with checks behind it: drafting a standard single-person reading, or a composite of a type already produced here, from a complete packet on an accepted template; repairing defects named at acceptance; checking a published document against its source; running the controller's written steps, live calls and filing; recording decisions. Independent measurements put it first on professional knowledge-work and office-deliverable evaluations from the middle level up, at about half the cost per task and 1.25 to 1.5 times the speed of the most capable model.
strong_lower_cost_model.not_for: The first report of a new type or template whose structure later reports copy, open-ended interpretation where no later check can catch an error, or work on which this model at a higher level has already fallen short.
examples: Write a standard single-person reading for a returning client on the accepted template
Fix four acceptance defects that each name a section and the failed requirement
Compare the published Google Doc with its accepted Markdown source and list every difference
